alignments.note: Aorist passive participle with its auxiliaries as rule 9 helpers, headed on the lexical verb.
Rule 106: the compound verb writes an English verb word of its own (buried), so the preposition realizing the governed dative's case rides with the governed pronoun.
ἐν → in.
Rule 23: the ASV writes no determiner for baptism, so this article has nothing to anchor.
βαπτισμῷ → baptism.
Rule 35: the ASV fuses preposition and relative into the portmanteau wherein, which spells both elements, so the pair is one aligned unit headed on the pronominal.
Rule 106: no source token answers to the συν- preverb here, so the supplied with him rides inside the compound verb's own unit, discontinuously around also (rule 15), headed on the verb word.

Rule 21: the article takes the English determiner and the preposition realizing the genitive relation rides with it, headed on the.

Rule 90: a substantival article before a participle rendered by the single word who takes that relativizer.

Rule 58: a substantival adjective takes the supplied determiner itself, headed on the adjective.

review_notes: The two συν- compounds are treated differently because the Greek differs, not the English: συνταφέντες governs an expressed dative αὐτῷ, so with him is that pronoun's under rule 106's case-government arm, while συνηγέρθητε governs nothing, so its supplied with him is the preverb's and stays inside the verb.
Both variants sit on r00-base and cover tokens the ASV translates.
